interface.signature: def criticalConnections(V: int, adj: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]

preconditions.expression: V >= 1 and all(0 <= u < V for edge in adj for u in edge)
preconditions.description: V is a positive integer, and all nodes in adjacency list edges are valid vertex indices (0 ≤ u < V).
The graph is connected (each node has at least one edge).

preconditions.expression: all(u <= v for u, v in (sorted(edge) for edge in adj))
preconditions.description: Each edge in the adjacency list is stored as a sorted pair (u, v) where u ≤ v.

postconditions.expression: all(len(edge) == 2 and edge[0] <= edge[1] for edge in return_value)
postconditions.description: Each critical connection is represented as a sorted pair of vertices (u, v) where u ≤ v.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= u < V and 0 <= v < V for edge in return_value for u, v in [edge])
postconditions.description: All vertices in the returned critical connections are valid vertex indices (0 ≤ u, v < V).

postconditions.expression: all(edge in [(u, v) for u in range(V) for v in adj[u] if u < v] for edge in return_value)
postconditions.description: Every returned critical connection is an actual edge in the input graph (undirected, sorted).

postconditions.expression: all(any(u == x and v == y or u == y and v == x for edge in return_value for u, v in [edge]) for x, y in return_value)
postconditions.description: No duplicate critical connections are returned (each edge appears at most once).

postconditions.expression: all(edge in return_value for edge in [(u, v) for u in range(V) for v in adj[u] if u < v] if not any(edge in [(x, y) for x in range(V) for y in adj[x] if x < y] for x, y in [(u, v)] if (u, v) != edge))
postconditions.description: The returned critical connections are exactly those edges whose removal disconnects the graph (no false positives).
The list of critical connections is sorted lexicographically (each edge sorted, then edges sorted).
